The root cause of the Kconfig warning is that `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` is being set or defaulted unconditionally, but this configuration option depends on `CONFIG_USERSPACE`. When a build is configured without userspace support, this results in an unsatisfied dependency warning.

The specific error log points to `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` being assigned the value '8', which originates from `tests/kernel/mem_protect/sys_sem/prj.conf`. This test can be built for platforms without userspace support, and in such cases, the unconditional setting causes the warning. The fix is to remove this line from the generic project configuration. The test will then rely on board-specific configurations to provide a suitable value for `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES`, which is the standard practice in Zephyr. Several boards already provide a default, and the test has a board-specific configuration for `pocketbeagle` that sets this value, indicating that relying on board configuration is the intended mechanism.

Additionally, several board `Kconfig.defconfig` files provide an unconditional default for `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES`. These are also incorrect and will produce similar warnings. The fix is to make these defaults conditional on `CONFIG_USERSPACE` being enabled.
